name: Surface Code Quantum Error Correction Below Threshold
description: Memory benchmark demonstrating a quantum error-correcting code operating below the fault-tolerant threshold on a superconducting processor. Google's team ran distance-3, -5 and -7 surface codes and showed that logical error rate per cycle drops by a factor Lambda each time code distance is increased by two, proving exponential error suppression with scale. Also ran a distance-29 repetition code. The distance-7 logical memory outlived its best physical qubit by a factor of 2.4, a first-of-its-kind result for superconducting hardware.
significance: First demonstration on superconducting hardware that increasing code distance reduces logical error exponentially — crossing the practical break-even point required for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation.

news.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
news.excerpt: Paper submitted to arXiv describing surface code quantum error correction experiments demonstrating exponential error suppression with increased code distance

news.title: IBM and UChicago Achieve Logical Error Rates 10× Below Physical in 70-Logical-Qubit Encoded Circuits
news.excerpt: IBM and UChicago ran 70 logical qubits with effective logical error rates 10× lower than physical qubit error rates, completing 2,415 logical two-qubit gates and 468 T gates. Results are released openly on the IBM Quantum Advantage Tracker.

news.title: USC and Quantum Elements Demonstrate Surface Code Scaling on IBM Heron Heavy-Hex Processors
news.excerpt: Quantum Elements and USC published a Nature Communications paper showing subthreshold surface-code scaling on IBM Heron processors despite their heavy-hex layout mismatching the code's square-grid geometry. The team combined a depth-minimising SWAP-based embedding with gap-aware dynamical decoupling to suppress idle-time errors, achieving below-threshold logical error-rate suppression as code distance increased.

news.title: USC And Quantum Elements Error Correction Technique Demonstrates Surface Code Scaling with Logical Qubits on IBM Heron
news.excerpt: Quantum Elements and the University of Southern California demonstrated that surface codes can achieve below-threshold error-rate scaling on IBM Heron processors with heavy-hex qubit connectivity, a geometry not natively suited to surface codes. The Nature Communications paper generalises surface-code QEC beyond hardware designed around square-grid connectivity.

news.title: NVIDIA Launches CUDA-Q Logical for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing at IEEE Quantum Week
news.excerpt: NVIDIA introduced CUDA-Q Logical, an open-source orchestration layer for designing and testing applications on fault-tolerant quantum computers with logical qubits. Fermilab cut fault-tolerant architecture development time from 5 months to 3 weeks; Infleqtion demonstrated qLDPC integration achieving up to 5× fewer physical data qubits than prevailing surface-code approaches.
